answer_text:
Let

\[
I=\int_{0}^{2\pi}\sin^2\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}+3e^{it}\right)\,dt.
\]

Set

\[
z=e^{it}.
\]

As \(t\) goes from \(0\) to \(2\pi\), \(z\) traverses the unit circle \(|z|=1\) once counterclockwise. Also,

\[
dz=ie^{it}\,dt=iz\,dt
\]

so

\[
dt=\frac{dz}{iz}.
\]

Define

\[
f(z)=\sin^2\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}+3z\right).
\]

Then

\[
I=\int_{0}^{2\pi} f(e^{it})\,dt
=\frac{1}{i}\oint_{|z|=1}\frac{f(z)}{z}\,dz.
\]

The function \(f(z)\) is entire, so the only singularity of \(f(z)/z\) inside the contour is a simple pole at \(z=0\). Its residue is

\[
\operatorname{Res}_{z=0}\frac{f(z)}{z}
=
\lim_{z\to 0} f(z)
=
\sin^2\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)
=
\frac14.
\]

By the residue theorem,

\[
\oint_{|z|=1}\frac{f(z)}{z}\,dz
=
2\pi i\cdot \frac14
=
\frac{\pi i}{2}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
I=\frac{1}{i}\cdot \frac{\pi i}{2}
=
\frac{\pi}{2}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{\pi}{2}}
\]
